conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions about your circumstances.

First, do you have any children that you're responsible for?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I do. I have two children - Alex, who's 13, and Blake, who's 15.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. It's great that you have two children, Alex (13) and Blake (15).

To assess your eligibility for Child Benefit, I need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

First, are you currently responsible for Alex and Blake? By this I mean, do they live with you, and are you responsible for their day-to-day care and financial support?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
Well, Alex lives with me at home, so yes, I'm responsible for them day-to-day. 

Blake doesn't live with me though - they live elsewhere. But I do help out financially with their upkeep.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that.

Just to understand Blake's situation better - when you say Blake lives elsewhere, could you tell me:

1. Where does Blake live (for example, with another parent, at boarding school, in their own accommodation, etc.)?
2. Are you contributing to their upkeep in the form of regular payments towards their maintenance?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Blake lives with their other parent. And yes, I contribute regularly - I help with their maintenance, about £26 a week.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information.

Now I need to ask about Alex and Blake's education and work status:

For Alex (age 13) - are they in full-time education?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex is in full-time education - they're at secondary school.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you. And what about Blake (age 15) - are they in full-time education or approved training?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Blake is still in full-time education as well - they're at school.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information.

Now I need to ask a few more questions:

Are you or your partner currently receiving Child Benefit for either Alex or Blake? (This includes if Blake's other parent is claiming Child Benefit for Blake.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I'm not currently receiving Child Benefit for either of them. And as far as I know, Blake's other parent isn't claiming it either.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that.

A few more questions to assess your eligibility:

1. Do you usually live in the UK?
2. Are Alex and Blake also usually living in the UK (I know Blake lives with their other parent, but is that still in the UK)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - I'm in Manchester. And yes, Blake lives in the UK too with their other parent.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information.

Just a couple more questions:

1. Are you or your partner subject to immigration control (for example, do you have any visa restrictions that say you have "no recourse to public funds")?

2. Regarding your income - are you or your partner earning over £50,000 per year? (This won't affect eligibility itself, but it may affect whether there's a tax charge to consider.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
No, neither of us has any immigration restrictions or visa issues - we can access public funds.

As for income, no, neither of us earns over £50,000 a year.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information.

Just one final question to complete my assessment:

You mentioned that Blake lives with their other parent. In general, only one person can claim Child Benefit for a child - usually the person the child lives with. However, there can be exceptions.

Can you confirm - does Blake's other parent provide the main day-to-day care for Blake, or is the care more equally shared between you both?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Blake's other parent provides the main day-to-day care - Blake lives with them full-time. I just help out with the financial side of things.

conversation.text:
## My Assessment

Thank you for answering all my questions. Based on the information you've provided, here's my assessment of your Child Benefit eligibility:

**For Alex (age 13): You ARE ELIGIBLE ✓**

Alex is under 16, in full-time education, lives with you, and you're responsible for their day-to-day care. You meet all the requirements to claim Child Benefit for Alex. Since you live in the UK with no immigration restrictions and no one else is claiming for Alex, you can make a claim.

**For Blake (age 15): You ARE NOT ELIGIBLE ✗**

While Blake is under 16 and in full-time education, they live with their other parent who provides the main day-to-day care. Under Child Benefit rules, only one person can claim for each child - usually the person the child lives with and who has main responsibility for their care. Even though you contribute financially to Blake's upkeep, you don't have main responsibility for their day-to-day care. Blake's other parent would be the appropriate person to claim Child Benefit for Blake if they wish to do so.

**What you should do:**

You can proceed to claim Child Benefit for Alex. Since your income is under £50,000, you won't face any tax charges related to Child Benefit.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit or your claim?
